The Typing Lab needs a physical keyboard. You can look around on a phone, but do the lessons and tests on a computer or a tablet with a keyboard.

Typing Lab

Every finger has its own keys. Learn them one row at a time, build accuracy first and speed second, and print your results when you are done. Everything happens here, so there is no outside site to sign up for.

A good way to practice

  1. 1Take a 1-minute testFind your starting point. Write down your net WPM and accuracy, or print the results.
  2. 2Work through the key lessonsGo in order. Do not look down; the hands and the keyboard on screen show the right finger.
  3. 3Practice a little every dayShort daily sessions beat one long session a week. Mix lessons, drills, and a game.
  4. 4Test again and printTake a timed test, compare with your first one, and submit the results page.

What is in the lab

  • Key lessons28 short lessons, from F and J to parentheses and @. Each drill uses only keys you have learned.
  • Timed tests1, 2, 3, or 5 minutes of medical office, front desk, customer service, or email writing. Scored in net WPM.
  • Workplace drillsPatient registration data entry, 10-key number entry, medical terms, and email punctuation.
  • GamesRace a pace car, and drag keys onto the fingers that press them.

How typing speed is scored

MeasureHow it is figuredExample: 1 minute, 200 characters, 6 errors left
Gross WPM(characters typed ÷ 5) ÷ minutes. A "word" is any 5 characters, including spaces.(200 ÷ 5) ÷ 1 = 40
Net WPMGross WPM − (uncorrected errors ÷ minutes)40 − (6 ÷ 1) = 34
Accuracycorrect characters ÷ characters typed × 100194 ÷ 200 × 100 = 97%

Which number do employers want?

When a job application or an employment typing test asks for your typing speed, give your net WPM and your accuracy. Net WPM already takes off your uncorrected errors, so it is the honest measure of usable work. Some employers set a speed together with an error limit instead. For example, U.S. federal job postings for office jobs often say a qualified typist can type 40 words per minute on a 5-minute sample with three or fewer errors. Every employer sets its own requirement, so read each posting.
